caveats: Question volume is not mastery coverage.
One opening geometry can support several question prompts; unique geometry is counted from canonical setup actors and puck only.
Domain signals are transparent text matches over current scenario metadata, not authored curriculum bindings.
Unseen delivery formats are backlog candidates, not automatic defects.

practice.note: Routine practice retains one optional reflection per scenario. Direct links can select another authored reflection. Authored counts below include all questions.

domains.name: Skating & Movement
domains.definition: Edges, agility, and footwork — the mobility that lets a player get to ice and execute reads in time.

concepts.name: Edges Balance
concepts.definition: Athletic stance, edge control, and balance on both feet.

concepts.name: Agility Mobility
concepts.definition: Crossovers, tight turns, pivots, and changing direction at speed.

concepts.name: Backward Transitions
concepts.definition: Backward skating and forward-to-backward transitions (pivots, mohawks, open-ups).

concepts.name: Deception With Feet
concepts.definition: The skating move itself: changes of pace and footwork fakes that unbalance a defender (the tool, not the when-to-use-it).

domains.name: Puck Skills
domains.definition: Controlling, protecting, moving, and shooting the puck — judged as decisions (when/where/whether), not just mechanics.

concepts.name: Puck Control
concepts.definition: Head-up stickhandling and carrying the puck under control.

concepts.name: Puck Protection
concepts.definition: Using body position and angle to shield the puck from a defender.

concepts.name: Passing
concepts.definition: Selecting a lane, timing, and weighting a pass; leading the receiver.

concepts.name: Receiving
concepts.definition: Catching and settling pucks, on the move, with a plan before they arrive.

concepts.name: Shooting
concepts.definition: Shot mechanics and selection; release, shooting in traffic and off the rush.

domains.mappingMethod: Signal map from actual scenario tags, topic, family and objective; this is an inventory aid, not an authored concept binding.

domains.name: Hockey Sense
domains.definition: The cognitive core: scanning, reading the play, and choosing the right option. RinkReads' anchor domain.

concepts.name: Scanning
concepts.definition: Head on a swivel: shoulder checks and visual exploration before and after receiving.

concepts.name: Reading The Play
concepts.definition: Anticipating what is about to happen from the cues on the ice.

concepts.name: Decision Making
concepts.definition: Selecting the best option — pass, shoot, carry, delay — for the situation; risk vs reward.

concepts.name: Time And Space
concepts.definition: Recognizing, creating, and exploiting time and space; when to slow down vs attack.

concepts.name: Creativity Under Pressure
concepts.definition: Finding the second or third option when the first is taken away — expanding the option set under pressure.

domains.name: Offensive Play
domains.definition: Creating and attacking with the puck and away from it — supporting, beating defenders, entering and extending offence.

concepts.name: Puck Carrier Options
concepts.definition: Reading the 1v1/2v1 as the carrier: attack, delay, pass, or protect.

concepts.name: Off Puck Support Offence
concepts.definition: Off-puck support: getting open, give-and-go timing, support angles/triangles/distance, and driving the net to be the best option for the carrier.

concepts.name: Attacking 1v1
concepts.definition: Beating a defender one-on-one: the decision of when to take them vs make a play.

concepts.name: Cycle And Possession
concepts.definition: Low cycle, F1/F2/F3 support, and extending offensive-zone possession.

concepts.name: Zone Entry
concepts.definition: Controlled vs dump entries; wide drive, delay, or cross based on the gap.

concepts.name: Odd Man Reads
concepts.definition: Reading odd-man situations as the attacker (2v1 / 3v2): pass, shoot, or drive based on the lone defender and the goalie.

concepts.name: Net Front Play
concepts.definition: Scoring-area reads off the puck: screen, tip/deflection, rebound timing, and finding the back door.

domains.name: Defensive Play
domains.definition: Taking away time and space — gaps, angles, positioning, and coverage to deny the read and recover the puck.

concepts.name: Gap Control
concepts.definition: Closing time and space on the rush by managing the gap — including the lone defender's read on a 2v1 (take the pass vs force the shot).

concepts.name: Angling Steering
concepts.definition: Steering the carrier to low-value ice with body angle and stick.

concepts.name: Defensive Side Positioning
concepts.definition: Individual net-side body position on one attacker: staying between your check and the net, body and stick on the inside.

concepts.name: Coverage Reads
concepts.definition: Team d-zone reads: which threat is yours, switching assignments, and weak-side awareness (the heavy switching content is U15+ refinement).

concepts.name: Stick And Body Detail
concepts.definition: Active stick in lanes, box-outs, and contain without over-committing.

domains.name: Transition & Compete
domains.definition: Switching between offence and defence and winning the puck — transition reads, breakouts, fore/backcheck, battles, talk.

concepts.name: Transition Reads
concepts.definition: The offence-to-defence switch and the first option after a change of possession.

concepts.name: Breakout And Regroup
concepts.definition: Support layers and options under forecheck; neutral-zone regroups.

concepts.name: Forecheck Pressure
concepts.definition: Angling and pressure to recover the puck; F1 reads.

concepts.name: Backcheck Recovery
concepts.definition: Picking up the right player and taking away the dangerous lane on the way back.

concepts.name: Battles And Compete
concepts.definition: 1v1 wall and net battles, loose-puck recovery, and resilience after a mistake.

sampleObjectives: Use an inside approach to influence a wide carrier without assuming a forced turnover.
Use a carrier-and-outlet read to choose an approach instead of following the puck alone.
Use an inside angle to influence the carrier away from the middle without guessing the outcome.
Protect the middle while retaining a route back toward the net.
Compare a carrying or shooting route with a pass using the defender and goalie cues.
Read the defender and teammate before continuing a two-on-one carry.
Choose a recovery relationship to an inside attacking threat.
Separate the carrier’s pressure from a second attacker’s route.
Choose a backcheck relationship for the uncovered attacker while a teammate pressures the puck.
Coordinate recovering help rather than duplicate wide pressure.
Track the second attacker after a puck-side handoff and keep the net-side lane in view.
Prepare a receiver and next option after a stated goalie outlet.
Prepare for a goalie outlet while treating the puck as loose until a player controls it.
Notice the forechecker before collecting a rim.
Recognize open ice behind the net and choose a support route that changes the forechecker’s angle
